report.interpretation: Open claims per adjuster by region, using the claims status as of the 2026-09-30 extract. The question is why Southeast is higher. I counted open claims divided by the adjusters currently employed in each region, and also by all adjusters who have handled claims in the region.
report.answer: The Southeast has about 51 open claims per active adjuster, against 11 in California, 14 in Texas and 18 in the North. Counting all six adjusters on record, it is 34 per adjuster. The data points to a staffing gap. Two of the six Southeast adjusters left in May 2026 (ADJ-016 on 05-01, ADJ-017 on 05-15). Their claims were all closed and they have no open claims, and no claims reported after their departures went to them. Since 05-16, the four remaining adjusters have taken on 137 new claims each, against 50 to 76 per adjuster elsewhere. As a result, 37% of Southeast claims reported since then are still open, against 18% to 24% in other regions. Average time to close for these claims rose from 32 to 37 days, while it fell in the other regions. The mix of claims is not the cause: bodily injury and liability claims are 9.3% of Southeast claims against 8% to 9% elsewhere. Note that recent claims are still incomplete and recent months are naturally more open.

findings.claim: Two Southeast adjusters left in May 2026. Since then the remaining four have received about 137 new claims each, nearly double the other regions, and a larger share of those claims is still open and slower to close.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Staffing: adjusters left and the remaining team absorbed the workload
hypotheses.evidence: Southeast is the only region with departures (2 of 6). The four remaining adjusters carry 137 new claims each since mid-May, and their open claims are 44 to 60 each.

hypotheses.hypothesis: More bodily injury and liability claims, which are slow to settle, in the Southeast
hypotheses.evidence: These causes are 9.3% of Southeast claims against 8.1% to 8.6% elsewhere, which can't explain a 3x gap.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Claim volume or a stale backlog from older claims
hypotheses.evidence: Southeast total claims (2,031) are in line with North (2,206) and Texas (1,654). Only 3 open claims were reported before 05-16, so the backlog is recent and not old claims.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Duplicated rows in the claims data
hypotheses.evidence: The data quality check found no repeated claim rows.

data_quality_issues.issue: The latest weeks are incomplete because claims are reported late, and recent claims are naturally still open (about 79% of September claims reported).
data_quality_issues.impact: Open counts for all regions are somewhat inflated by recent claims, but this affects every region equally and does not explain the Southeast gap.

proposed_actions.title: Backfill Southeast adjuster capacity
proposed_actions.reason: Two of six Southeast adjusters left in May 2026, leaving four with about 51 open claims each. Consider hiring or temporarily redistributing claims from other regions.

open_questions: Is a Southeast hiring plan already under way? Would cross-region help be allowed, since adjusters work only in one region?
